content: Clotrimazole, when used on mucous membranes, is an azole antifungal agent approved by the FDA for treating tinea pedis (athlete's foot), tinea cruris (jock itch), and tinea corporis (ringworm). Common side effects include nausea and vomiting. Adult Indications and Dosage For antifungal treatment in adults: Clean and thoroughly dry the affected area before application. Apply a thin layer of the product to the affected area twice daily (morning and night) or as directed by a physician. Supervise children during use. For athlete's foot, pay special attention to the spaces between the toes, wear well-fitting, ventilated shoes, and change shoes and socks at least once daily. Use daily for 4 weeks for athlete's foot and ringworm, and for 2 weeks for jock itch. If the condition persists beyond this duration, consult a doctor. This product is not effective for fungal infections of the scalp or nails. Off-label adult use is limited, but one guideline-supported regimen involves applying 5 grams once weekly for 2 weeks. Pediatric Indications and Dosage There is limited information regarding FDA-approved or off-label use of clotrimazole (mucous membrane) in pediatric patients. Contraindications Clotrimazole is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity to the drug. Warnings For external use only. If swallowed, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Do not use on children under 2 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Avoid contact with the eyes. Discontinue use and consult a doctor if irritation occurs or if there is no improvement within 2 weeks. Keep out of reach of children. Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Experience: Common gastrointestinal side effects include nausea and vomiting. Postmarketing Experience: No information is available regarding postmarketing adverse events. Overdosage Information on clotrimazole overdose is limited. In cases of suspected overdose or poisoning, contact the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) immediately.
